title: Zulu ball, Irma Thomas and being asked back
summary: Irma Thomas wishes blacks would hire her; the Zulus ask him to play their ball after being dissatisfied with others.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Because you don't work, you know, to black audiences, I'm saying, you were working to whites, did blacks ever tell you, you know, why don't you play for your own kind?

No. No, no, never, no. You never get that. The only thing, and I'm going to tell you the exact words that Irma said, she said, I wish some blacks would hire me. But they don't even call Irma. Now, she played for the Zulus. And they were highly dissatisfied with her.

They said she didn't reach them. And I got this direct from them. Now, the gentleman called me to play for the Zulus. And I can look out here and tell you what date. To play for the Zulus on the 27th of February this year. He wanted, and this is the Autocrat Circle.

He asked me, would I play their ball? He said, they were dissatisfied with the Neville brothers. Uh-huh. They want me. So, I said, well, you know, I played for the Autocrat Circle. I said, but, and I said, let me tell you, because this is a money thing now I'm thinking about. I said, if you call me any time, and we get together and sign a contract, and agree on the money, I said, sure I'll play. Whereas they give me time to tell the Autocrat Circle I have another engagement, but I'll only be going for one year. And it's money. I'll take it. So, I'm waiting for him to call me because he said, every year, I'm, every year I'm recommend to play for the Zulus ball. Every year. But every year they call me, and I'm, I've been playing for the Autocrat Circle now about eight years. And he said, but every way he called me, he said, so he called me, it was two weeks ago he called me. So, I told him, yeah, he said, well look, he said, the first of April, he said, I will get back to you. He said, I'm going to let you know. He said, but I think you'll get it. He said, if you accept it, I think you'll get it for me. And you see, this is what's happening with all of the, see like the Illinois, the young Illinois, I already played for the young Illinois. I don't play any ball, but I play everything else. And Mr. Houston plays all these things. But, they are not satisfied with Houston, because he is too uptight. And they say, what Mr. Houston, what he's playing, he's trying to play for young people. Whereas, I play for all the people. And Mr. Houston is trying to change this thing, play for the young people. And the people who, with the money in the pocket, who happen to be the older people, is getting dissatisfied with him. So they all want, everybody want me. I love it. Yes sir. We were talking about carnival music. What other music did you hear?
